title: CAPTCHA recognition with a deep CNN
highlights: Generates its own dataset of text CAPTCHAs with the Python captcha library and a TrueType font.
Preprocessing with PIL and OpenCV: grayscale conversion, contour finding and bounding rectangles around each character.
A sequential convolutional network in Keras and TensorFlow classifies the extracted characters.
Reached 0.696 accuracy, about 70%, with accuracy and loss curves tracked during training.

details.label: The question
details.body: Text CAPTCHAs still guard many sites, and deep learning can now defeat many of them. Breaking them is the fastest way to find out which properties actually protect: distortion, noise, rotation, variable length, touching characters.

details.label: Pipeline
details.body: Each CAPTCHA image is converted to grayscale and OpenCV finds the contours of the characters. Bounding rectangles around each contour isolate the characters. Each one goes to a CNN built with Keras on TensorFlow, and the character predictions are compared with the CAPTCHA's true text.

details.label: Evaluation
details.body: Accuracy is the fraction of CAPTCHAs recognized correctly, 0.696 here. The report also tracks accuracy and loss curves.

details.label: Where it stops
details.body: The test set is generated CAPTCHAs, which are cleaner than real ones. The planned next step was larger and noisier CAPTCHAs with more symbols.

summary: A CNN that reads text CAPTCHAs (letters and digits) and reaches about 70% on its test set. The aim was to break them and to learn what makes CAPTCHAs resistant. Course project, team of three.
